utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is case number IT-02-60-PT, the Prosecutor versus Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Peter McCloskey for the Prosecution, with Janet Stewart, our case manager, Stefan Waespi, and Anne Davis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I, Veselin Londrovic, counsel; and Mr. Stefan Kirsch, my co-counsel, and Ms. Vesna Anic, who is our interpreter, are representing the accused Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. This hearing is a continuation of the proceedings held yesterday. We noticed that there are some adjustments of the plea agreement by both parties in light of yesterday's discussion. First of all, I would like to express our appreciation to both parties for their effort in reaching this agreement, especially after yesterday's hearing. Now could we ask both parties to brief us on those adjustments, and then we might ask some questions. For the Prosecution, Mr. McCloskey, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We dealt specifically with the issue, first of all, that I believe the Court was very concerned about, and that was in paragraph 4(b), where we have agreed with counsel to, if the plea is accepted, that at that time we will move to dismiss without prejudice the remaining charges against Mr. Nikolic. And there's no problem with that, and all sides agree, and I think from our discussions yesterday we did bring out that that was something that is no longer necessary in this Tribunal with the protections that this Tribunal has. So that was number one. Then the next part was the section that had to do with the nature of the charges, where we, in 5(1) we not only as originally deleted references to "genocide or complicity in genocide" but also deleted the references to the other charges. Initially it was thought by both parties that those references were included within persecutions, but upon closer look, while those references are part of persecutions, they were in the indictment as part of the other charges, as you correctly pointed out, and so that we have now cleared that up by deleting them and so that Mr. Nikolic will not be pleading to anything related to those other charges. And so we were able to work together well, like we have been over the past few weeks, and I believe all parties are satisfied with the -- with the agreement as it -- as it now stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could I turn to the Defence team. Are there any observations, comments on that particular point?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you agree with that -- those adjustments in the plea agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We have told our client about the changes. He has accepted them. Everything has been explained to him, and everything was done in agreement with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Any questions from the Judges? I see none. Now I would like to address the accused, Mr. Nikolic, at this stage. Mr. Nikolic, the Trial Chamber would like to find out from you whether you understand the details of this plea agreement you entered into with the Prosecution. THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. My lawyers have explained to me all the details contained in the agreement, and I fully understand the clauses of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This Trial Chamber also would like to find out from you, when entering into this plea agreement, you understand that this Trial Chamber is not bound to accept the range of sentence agreed to by you and the Prosecution. THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC: [Interpretation] Yes. That part of the agreement was explained to me too, and I am quite clear about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As we understand that you have already discussed with your lawyer about the details of this plea agreement, did he advise you of the consequences of pleading guilty to count 5, that is, persecution? THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC: [Interpretation] Yes, he did, Your Honour. My lawyers -- or rather, Mr. Londrovic and Mr. Kirsch told me about all the details and consequences of the -- emanating from the agreement and the consequences of my pleading guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We would like to know whether you were threatened or coerced in any way to make this agreement. Was it entirely made by you voluntarily? THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can say here that no threats were addressed to me during the discussions about the agreement or here that nobody forced anything on me and that this agreement is an act of my goodwill, or rather, I made my own decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well, then. This Trial Chamber would like to put the count to you so that you can plea as otherwise and according to your own free will. That is count 5 of the charges as detailed in the plea agreement. Are you ready for that? THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How do you plead to count 5 of the amended indictment charging you with persecution as a crime against humanity; guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead guilty on count 5, that is, the charge that relates to persecutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very well. This Trial Chamber records a plea of guilty of count 5, persecution, by the accused. This Trial Chamber has considered the particulars of the facts in the plea agreement and is satisfied that they do form sufficient factual basis for finding the accused guilty on the count. Therefore, makes a finding of guilty and enters the conviction for count 5, persecution, against the accused, Mr. Nikolic. We also accept the plea agreement with the understanding that the Prosecutor will move to dismiss without prejudice to either party the remaining charges against Momir Nikolic set out in the indictment. You may sit down, please. THE ACCUSED NIKOLIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will issue orders relating further proceedings in due course. Now we could move to the next stage, about a possible date for hearing of sentencing. And I would like to find out from both parties how they intend to make their submissions on sentencing. Mr. McCloskey, can you indicate how much time you think you need for the submission of your files.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Given the impending trial, it would be nice to have at least two months to get something together for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could I turn to the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence believes that our preparation for the sentencing hearing - because earlier we didn't pay much attention to that; we were getting prepared for the trial - but we believe we might need about three months to prepare properly for the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems to me that it's very difficult at this stage to set a particular date for that hearing because we have to get the submissions from both parties. Of course, this Trial Chamber is in a very difficult position at this moment. Like Mr. McCloskey said, we have a big case pending; at the same time, the Judges are involved in other obligations, for instance, the judgement of another case. But I hope that the parties will submit their filings as soon as possible because we have to move forward. The Trial Chamber will issue a scheduling order on the matters of further hearings in these proceedings. Now it's very difficult to fix a particular date. We hope we could have it before the summer recess, but which seems to me is very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any observations at this stage from both parties? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, we have no comments. Only we'd like to ask you, in your scheduling order, to see that we do it after the summer recess, and I do hope you will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You mean -- what do you mean by "after summer recess"? You mean the filing of the submissions or the hearing on the sentencing issues? I have to make it clear on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the hearing. And as for the submissions, we can submit that earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think that's all. We are adjourned.
